findings.title: Plugin request logs drop traceID
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware used to append traceID to every "Plugin Request Completed" line (eventName=grafana-data-egress) via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false), which includes the ID even when the span is not sampled. That call was removed with the tracing import. The attributes now stored by ContextualLoggerMiddleware are only endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname, and the new plugins/log FromContext wrapper does not add a trace ID either. Completion logs will no longer carry traceID, so these egress events cannot be correlated with traces.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards recorded logs
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext ignores the receiver and returns NewTestLogger(), a separate logger whose InfoLogs/WarnLogs/ErrorLogs/DebugLogs stay empty. LoggerMiddleware now emits "Plugin Request Completed" through m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info rather than m.logger.Info. Tests that inject a TestLogger and assert on InfoLogs will see zero calls even when the line was logged, because the write lands on the discarded child. FromContext should return the same TestLogger (or a child that records into the same Logs) so this path is observable.

findings.title: No test locks the split logging contract
findings.body: ContextualLoggerMiddleware is new and has no tests, and LoggerMiddleware no longer puts pluginId, endpoint, user, or datasource on the log line itself; those fields now exist only if this middleware ran first and FromContext reads them back. The renamed metrics test only checks Prometheus counters. Nothing installs the production order (contextual logger outside the request logger) and asserts that "Plugin Request Completed" still contains those fields, so a reorder or a dropped attribute would ship without a failing test.
